# T004.1 — Add ASP.NET Core integration-test harness

## Summary

Added a separate net10.0 xUnit/WebApplicationFactory project for the new, currently empty host. Reviewed its factory, offline JWKS handler, project references and solution registration. Its four tests exercise host startup and fixture HTTP behavior, **not** any migrated route or token validation.

## Changes (files and why)

- `DescopeSampleApp.IntegrationTests/DescopeSampleApp.IntegrationTests.csproj` — net10.0 xUnit test project referencing only the new ASP.NET Core host, with the WebApplicationFactory and test SDK packages.
- `DescopeSampleApp.IntegrationTests/OfflineHostFixture.cs` — reusable in-process host factory; injectable in-memory JWKS JSON, default and named JWKS HttpClient wiring, and an HTTP handler rejecting every URL or method except GET of the declared fixture JWKS URL.
- `DescopeSampleApp.IntegrationTests/HostIntegrationTests.cs` — one real host startup/probe test and three tests of the offline handler and factory-provided HTTP clients.
- `DescopeSampleApp.Core/Program.cs` — public partial entry point for WebApplicationFactory without adding application routes.
- `DescopeSampleApp.sln` — registers the new test project for Debug and Release builds.
- This progress note — scope, executed tests and remaining coverage gaps.

## Decisions (rationale and sources)

- Keep the existing System.Web project unchanged and the net48 characterization project separate. The approved T004 plan requires a separate net10.0 test project and a host-start test before routes are ported; the web-migration skill calls for in-process HTTP characterization when migrated routes become available.
- The probe asserts 404 only for a deliberately non-migrated sentinel path; it proves factory startup, not compatibility for `/`, `/api/sample`, MVC or Web Forms routes.
- The fixture's explicit direct/default/`Jwks` registrations reject unexpected outbound requests on those clients. Future validator HTTP wiring must use an overridden, verified client; this fixture does not prove that arbitrary newly named clients or raw `new HttpClient()` calls cannot reach the network. The current host has no JWKS consumer.

## Validation (commands and results)

- `msbuild -restore -p:RestorePackagesConfig=true -p:Configuration=Release -m -nologo -v:minimal` — PASS (exit 0); all four solution projects built. Existing legacy NU1902 (two jQuery advisories) and MSB3247 assembly-binding warning remain.
- `dotnet test --no-build -c Release` — PASS (exit 0); **23 net48 characterization tests plus 4 net10 integration tests executed: 27 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- Lint: none configured.
- Setup: Windows MSBuild builds the unchanged net48 legacy app and both test projects plus the net10 host; the exact full-solution `dotnet test --no-build -c Release` executes the already built assemblies. WebApplicationFactory hosts the new application in-process; fixture HTTP calls use an in-memory handler and require no external service, container or credentials.

## Follow-ups and risks

- T005 must add deterministic signed token/key fixtures and verify the validator's actual injected JWKS path with offline valid/invalid/expired-token tests; the present empty JWKS fixture is scaffolding, not token coverage.
- HTTP equivalence for Web API, MVC and the Razor Pages remains unverified until those routes are implemented and characterized in subsequent tasks. No legacy behavior, route or CI/deployment configuration changed here.
